window: Covering reporting published since the Sept 21 edition, roughly Sept 20-22. No new SOUTHCOM vessel strike was found in this window beyond the Sept 19 Caribbean strike already logged Sept 20, so the campaign's running total of 69 strikes and at least 231 deaths carries forward unchanged; instead, the major development was a Sept 21 United Nations report finding reasonable grounds that the strike campaign constitutes crimes against humanity, covered in the ongoing section. Several candidates were checked and dropped: a widely surfaced claim of a 3.2-million-pill Thai methamphetamine seizure in Lampang/Chiang Rai on Sept 21 could not be traced to any real article and appears to be a search-summary fabrication conflating unrelated older Chiang Rai Times seizure stories, so it was excluded entirely; a Brazilian 'largest cocaine seizure in history' Operation Timber Shield story recirculating this week actually dates to June 2026, not September; a Tijuana/Otay Mesa 'trailero' meth-and-fentanyl arrest dated Sept 21 matches the same tonnage and fentanyl weight as the Sept 19 Tijuana customs-dog seizure already logged, so it was treated as the same event rather than new; a Washington County, Florida meth bust ('Operation King of the Hill') was announced Sept 11-12, outside this window; a Martin County, Florida cocaine bust with kilogram figures was from mid-August; and Ecuador's Manta curfew campaign (2.9 t cocaine, already logged Sept 20-21) had only a vague three-day cumulative figure this window with no clearly new, separately countable seizure, so nothing further was added to the tally for it. Colombia's Turbo/Antioquia coast guard capture and the Colombian Navy's two-Caribbean-operation announcement were confirmed via multiple outlets to be the same combined event (4.69 t, 8 people) rather than two separate seizures.
